1→//! Provides `SignedBeaconBlock` verification logic.
     2→//!
     3→//! Specifically, it provides the following:
     4→//!
     5→//! - Verification for gossip blocks (i.e., should we gossip some block from the network).
     6→//! - Verification for normal blocks (e.g., some block received on the RPC during a parent lookup).
     7→//! - Verification for chain segments (e.g., some chain of blocks received on the RPC during a
     8→//!   sync).
     9→//!
    10→//! The primary source of complexity here is that we wish to avoid doing duplicate work as a block
    11→//! moves through the verification process. For example, if some block is verified for gossip, we
    12→//! do not wish to re-verify the block proposal signature or re-hash the block. Or, if we've
    13→//! verified the signatures of a block during a chain segment import, we do not wish to verify each

    28→//!             |              |

   420→impl ExecutionPayloadError {
   421→    pub fn penalize_peer(&self) -> bool {
   422→        // This match statement should never have a default case so that we are
   423→        // always forced to consider here whether or not to penalize a peer when
   424→        // we add a new error condition.
   425→        match self {
   426→            // The peer has nothing to do with this error, do not penalize them.
   427→            ExecutionPayloadError::NoExecutionConnection => false,
   428→            // The peer has nothing to do with this error, do not penalize them.
   429→            ExecutionPayloadError::RequestFailed(_) => false,
   430→            // An honest optimistic node may propagate blocks which are rejected by an EE, do not
   431→            // penalize them.
   432→            ExecutionPayloadError::RejectedByExecutionEngine { .. } => false,
   433→            // This is a trivial gossip validation condition, there is no reason for an honest peer
   434→            // to propagate a block with an invalid payload time stamp.
   435→            ExecutionPayloadError::InvalidPayloadTimestamp { .. } => true,
   436→            // An honest optimistic node may propagate blocks with an invalid terminal PoW block, we
   437→            // should not penalized them.
   438→            ExecutionPayloadError::InvalidTerminalPoWBlock { .. } => false,
   439→            // This condition is checked *after* gossip propagation, therefore penalizing gossip
   440→            // peers for this block would be unfair. There may be an argument to penalize RPC
   441→            // blocks, since even an optimistic node shouldn't verify this block. We will remove the
   442→            // penalties for all block imports to keep things simple.

   445→            ExecutionPayloadError::InvalidTerminalBlockHash { .. } => false,

   447→            ExecutionPayloadError::UnverifiedNonOptimisticCandidate => false,
